newsitem.title: USA: Simpson to get children back, but when is unsure.
newsitem.headline: Simpson to get children back, but when is unsure.

text.p: O.J. Simpson was awarded custody of his children after a bitter fight against the parents of his slain ex-wife, but just when they will return to his mansion was unclear on Saturday.

The ruling by a family court judge in Orange County late on Friday afternoon to return permanent custody of Sydney, 11, and Justin, 8, to Simpson is likely to be appealed by the children's maternal grandparents, who have looked after them for the last 2-1/2 years.
Denise Brown, the sister of Nicole Brown Simpson, said in a tearful interview on CNN's Larry King Live on Friday night that there would be an appeal.
"This is the decision my parents have made," she said.
Louis and Judith Brown, who were granted visitation rights by Orange County Judge Nancy Wieben Stock in her ruling, said they received the news with "great sadness and concern."

Simpson signed temporary guardianship of the children, whom he had by Nicole Brown Simpson, over to the Browns after his arrest on June 17, 1994, and they have lived with them since then in the Orange County coastal community of Dana Point, south of Los Angeles.

The Browns' lawyer, Natasha Roit, said that under the judge's ruling, the children can spend the upcoming Christmas and New Year holidays with Simpson, but they cannot be moved permanently out of the Browns' home before Jan. 10. Stock scheduled a hearing then on the Browns' request to stay the children's departure pending an appeal.

Shortly after Stock's ruling, Simpson -- who was acquitted in October 1995 of the June 1994 murders of his ex-wife and her friend Ronald Goldman -- issued a statement saying, "We are all so very grateful to have the children home again where they want to be."

The former football star is currently the defendant in civil wrongful death lawsuit brought against him by the families of the victims. That trial, in a Santa Monica courtroom, was in recess for the holidays and will resume on Jan. 6.

In her ruling, Stock said "As evidence of the children's lack of fear of their father, at least one child has expressed an unequivocal preference to be returned to the immediate custody of (the) father.

"The other child has declined to state a preference to the court appointed psychologist, but has stated in positive tones the strong bonds the child has with the father's neighbourhood and the child's friends."

Stock said she found testimony about Simpson slapping his ex-wife on at least three occasions in the 1980s to be true, and also found that "the relationship reached a fearful crescendo on Jan. 1, 1989 when Simpson was arrested and charged with domestic violence."
But although Simpson admitted fault in the incident "resulting in injury to Nicole, the court does not find his admission to be entirely revealing."

In the civil case, Simpson denied on the witness stand last month ever having hit, slapped or struck his ex-wife. Stock, in her ruling, said a review of Simpson's history with the children "does not yield a picture of a man who has in the past or is likely in the future to lose control of himself in such a manner as to emotionally or physically harm his two young children."
